name: Floyd County, Kentucky
region: Floyd County and the Big Sandy valley in eastern Kentucky, with Hand in Hand Ministries in Auxier

families.label: An older homeowner in a Floyd County hollow: fixed income, a manufactured home beside a creek
families.incomeNote: Her check keeps coming, so time off costs her no pay. The extra costs are what hurt.
families.leaveNote: Kentucky has no state paid sick or family leave (KFF 2025).
families.health: Medicaid is the main coverage for 38.1%; uninsured 5.2% (2024). Drive times to care: not yet sourced.

loanOptions.label: A licensed installment loan
loanOptions.note: Installment loans: up to 3% a month under $5,000 (KRS 286.4-530).

loanOptions.label: A payday loan
loanOptions.note: Payday: $15 per $100 for two weeks, about 391% a year (our arithmetic); $600 most (KRS 286.9-100, 2026).

loanOptions.label: A credit card, if her credit allows

families.lifeInsNote: No local life-insurance figure. Social Security survivor benefits reach 1,115 widow(er)s and parents and 595 children in Floyd County (Dec 2025).

families.label: A Denver family with a salaried parent
families.leaveNote: Colorado FAMLI: up to 12 paid weeks; about 70% of pay at this salary (90% up to half the state average wage, 50% above).
families.health: Insured through work. Colorado's uninsured rate is 5.9% (2025).
families.loanNote: Average credit-card rate, 21.19% a year (Federal Reserve, Q3 2026).
families.lifeInsNote: 71% of U.S. households earning $150,000+ own life insurance (LIMRA 2024).

families.label: A Denver family whose father does day labor for cash
families.leaveNote: FAMLI needs $2,500 in reported Colorado wages; cash day labor often has none.
families.health: Coverage is uncertain; Denver Health is the city's safety net.
families.loanNote: Colorado caps small loans at 36% a year (Prop 111, 2018).
families.lifeInsNote: 31% of U.S. households earning under $50,000 own life insurance (LIMRA 2024).
